title: Migration Waves
description: A schematic diagram of labeled region tiles (not a map) with South Asia in the center. A year slider from 1830 to 2020 lights up arcs for the major waves of South Asian migration: indenture to Mauritius, the Caribbean and Fiji; East Africa; the early United States; Britain; the 1972 Uganda expulsion to Britain; the Gulf; and the United States after 1965. A card gives each wave's dates, cause and one sourced fact.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Migration
South Asian diaspora
World history
Immigration history
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Identify the major waves of South Asian migration and when each was active.
Explain the main cause of each wave, from plantation labor after the abolition of slavery to the Gulf oil boom and the US Immigration Act of 1965.
Recognize that some migrations, such as the 1972 move from Uganda to Britain, did not start in South Asia.
prerequisites: Knowing the eight countries of South Asia
A basic idea of the British Empire and Indian independence in 1947
keyQuestions: When did the first large waves of South Asian migration begin, and why?
Which waves were tied to the British Empire?
Why did South Asian migration to the United States grow so much after 1965?
misconceptions: South Asians only came to the United States after 1965.
Indenture was simply voluntary migration for better jobs.
The South Asian diaspora is all Indian.
Every migration started directly from South Asia.
controls: Click or tap a region tile
